title: The World Cup Is in Your Backyard. On Friday Night, America Kicks Off at SoFi.
excerpt: The USA hosts Paraguay in its 2026 World Cup opener at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood — the heart of Southern California's Indian community. Here is what NRIs need to know.
body:
On Friday evening at 6 PM Pacific Time, the United States will walk onto the pitch at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, to open its 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign against Paraguay. For the estimated 700,000 Indian Americans living in the Greater Los Angeles area, the biggest sporting event on earth is not on a screen thousands of miles away. It is a thirty-minute drive from Artesia.

## The Match

The USA enters as favourites in Group D, drawn alongside Paraguay, Australia, and Türkiye. Head coach Mauricio Pochettino, the Argentine who took over in September 2024, has built a squad around athleticism, a high press, and Christian Pulisic's creative brilliance. The 26-man roster features players from AC Milan, Juventus, PSV, Crystal Palace, and Bayer Leverkusen — a generation of Americans who have earned their place at Europe's biggest clubs.

Paraguay, managed by Gustavo Alfaro, are a different kind of dangerous. They went unbeaten in eight matches during qualifying, including wins over Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay. They conceded only 14 goals across 18 CONMEBOL qualifiers. Alfaro's side does not come to trade goals. They come to frustrate, absorb, and punish.

Pochettino is expected to deploy a 3-4-2-1 formation, with Chris Richards anchoring the back three and Pulisic operating behind Folarin Balogun. Weston McKennie and Tyler Adams will control the midfield engine. For Paraguay, key forward Julio Enciso will miss the match through injury, but Miguel Almirón remains a threat on the counter.

The USA's recent form has been a mixed bag. A 3-2 win over Senegal showed firepower and resilience. A 2-1 loss to Germany in the final warm-up exposed defensive fragility, though Antonee Robinson's goal was a highlight. The pattern is clear: this American team can hurt anyone but can also be hurt.

## The SoFi Factor

SoFi Stadium, which hosted the Super Bowl in 2022 and will host the 2028 Olympics opening ceremony, holds 70,000 fans for football. On Friday night, it will be the loudest it has ever been for a soccer match.

For Indian Americans in Southern California, this is unprecedented proximity to global sport. The 2026 World Cup is not just happening in the United States — it is happening in their metro area, across their time zones, in stadiums they drive past on the 405. The USA plays two of its three group matches at SoFi (Paraguay on June 12, Türkiye on June 25). If they advance, the Round of 32 returns to Los Angeles as well.

## How to Watch

- **TV (English):** FOX
- **Streaming (English):** Tubi (free), FOX Sports app
- **TV (Spanish):** Telemundo
- **Streaming (Spanish):** Peacock
- **Kick-off:** Friday, June 12 at 6:00 PM PT / 9:00 PM ET

For NRIs on the East Coast, the 9 PM start is prime-time viewing. For those on the West Coast, bars across the South Bay, Fremont, and Cupertino are already organising watch parties. Several Indian restaurants in the Edison, New Jersey corridor and in Artesia, California, have announced World Cup screening events.

## The Bigger Picture

Mexico opened the tournament on Thursday with a 2-0 win over South Africa at the Estadio Azteca in front of 80,824 fans. Julián Quiñones scored in the ninth minute and Raúl Jiménez added a second in the 67th. It was a match that eventually saw both teams reduced — ten men against nine — but Mexico's quality told. The tone has been set: this World Cup is already delivering drama.

On Friday, Canada hosts Bosnia and Herzegovina in Toronto at 3 PM ET before the USA's evening kickoff. The three co-host nations all play within 48 hours of each other. By Saturday night, the tournament's opening narrative will be written.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For a community that often feels split between the cricket pitch and the football stadium, the 2026 World Cup offers something rare: a chance to cheer for the country you live in, at a venue you can reach by car, at a time when you are still awake. Thirty-two years after the USA last hosted the World Cup, the tournament is back. And this time, the Indian diaspora is not watching from the margins. They are in the stadium, in the watch parties, and on the group chats — fully, unmistakably part of it.

*Sources: FOX Sports, NBC Sports, FIFA, RotoWire, USA Today*
